entities.name: Bacurius III of Iberia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bacurius III (Bakur III) was the final Chosroid monarch of Iberia (modern-day Georgia), reigning from approximately 574 CE until his death in 580 CE. His brief tenure marked the definitive end of a sovereign Iberian monarchy that had persisted for over six centuries, initiating an era of direct Sassanid Persian rule over the region. His significance lies not in his individual achievements, but in his historical position as the last vestige of an independent Iberian kingship, a role that brought the ancient kingdom under the direct administrative control of the powerful Sassanian Empire, fundamentally altering the geopolitical landscape of the Caucasus for generations.

Ascending to the throne amidst the protracted Byzantine-Sassanid Wars (572–591 CE), Bacurius III inherited a kingdom already heavily influenced and often contested by these two great powers. While specific details of his rule are scarce in extant historical records, it is understood that he presided over a realm whose autonomy was increasingly nominal, particularly in the face of aggressive Sassanid expansionism under Shah Khosrow I Anushirvan and his successor Hormizd IV. Unlike earlier Iberian kings who skillfully navigated between Rome/Byzantium and Persia, Bacurius III's position was precarious, as the Sassanids sought to consolidate their control over strategic Caucasian territories. His reign concluded with his death in 580 CE, an event the Sassanid authorities exploited to formally abolish the Iberian monarchy, rather than permit the succession of another Chosroid prince.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bacurius III's reign marks the definitive end of the ancient Iberian monarchy, leading to direct Sassanid rule and a profound geopolitical shift in the Caucasus. This event established a precedent for foreign domination that shaped the region for centuries.
